sounds.intro: Azerbaijani is written in the Latin alphabet and is spelled almost exactly as it sounds. There are no genders and no articles. The stress is usually on the last syllable. Learn the special letters first.
rows: a short, flat "uh", like the "a" in "about"
say "oh" with rounded lips, like German "ö"
say "ee" with rounded lips, like German "ü"
a hard "g" made far back in the throat
soft, almost silent, makes the vowel before it longer
notes: Vowel harmony: back vowels (a, ı, o, u) and front vowels (e, ə, i, ö, ü) are not mixed in one word. Suffixes follow the same rule.

grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Azerbaijani often drops the pronoun, because the verb ending shows who is speaking. There is no he / she difference: "o" means both.

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: Add -lar or -lər, by vowel harmony. After a number, the noun stays singular: iki kitab (two book).

grammar.title: To be: -am, -san, -dır
text: There is no separate verb "to be". Add an ending to the noun or adjective. After a vowel, the ending changes: tələbə-yəm (I am a student).

grammar.title: Var and yox: have, there is
text: Azerbaijani says "my X exists" (var) or "my X does not exist" (yox). The ending shows the owner: -ım / -im (my), -ın / -in (your), -ı / -i (his).

grammar.title: Present tense: -ır
text: Verb stem + -ır / -ir / -ur / -ür + person ending. Gəlmək (to come): gəl-ir-əm.

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: The verb goes last. Order: who, where or when, what, verb. Azerbaijani has no articles: "kitab" means "a book" or "the book".

grammar.title: Negation
text: Put -mı / -mi / -mu / -mü after the verb stem: gedirəm (I go), getmirəm (I do not go). For nouns use "deyil" (is not). "Yox" means "there is not". Always compare with the positive form.
ex: I do not have a car
he does not work on Sundays

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: Add the little word -mı / -mi / -mu / -mü after the word you are asking about. It is the same for every question.

grammar.title: Question words
text: Question words stand where the answer would stand.

grammar.title: Possessives and liking
text: Endings go on the noun: -ım / -im (my), -ın / -in (your), -ı / -i (his / her). To say you like something, use "xoşuma gəlir" (it comes to my liking).

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: sən (informal): friends, family, children. siz (formal): strangers, older people, work. Verb endings change: -san / -sən (informal), -sınız / -siniz (formal).

grammar.title: Past and future (simple)
text: Past: -dı / -di / -du / -dü + person ending (getdim = I went). Future: -acaq / -əcək + person ending (gedəcəyəm = I will go).

grammar.title: Commands
text: Informal: the bare verb stem. Formal: add -ın / -in (gəlin). To forbid, add -ma / -mə after the stem.

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: Can: verb + a bilmək (üzə bilirəm, I can swim). Must: "lazımdır" or "gərək" (needed). Want: istəyirəm (verb + -maq).
ex: I do not want to eat

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: Azerbaijani uses endings, not words in front: -da / -də (in, on, at), -a / -ə (to), -dan / -dən (from), -ın / -in (of).
ex: the book is on the table
the cat is under the table
the shop is next to the bank
the park is near the station
the key is in the bag

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: Put "daha" before the adjective for "more": daha böyük. For "the most" put "ən" before it: ən böyük. "Than" is -dan / -dən.
